podcast.title: Founding and Vision (1983)
podcast.body: Creation Records was a British independent label founded in 1983 by Alan McGee, Dick Green, and Joe Foster. Their core vision was to provide a platform for new bands with risky sounds that deviated from commercial standards, aiming to foster experimental and non-mainstream music. "Fue un sello independiente británico fundado en 1983 por Alan McGee, Dick Dean y Joe Foster, cuya visión era darca vida a nuevas bandas con sonidos arriesgados y alejados de el estándar comercial."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: El disco imposible: La historia de Loveless y My Bloody Valentine

podcast.title: Discovery of Oasis (1993)
podcast.body: Headed by Alan McGee, Creation Records, an indie label, discovered Oasis on May 31, 1993, at King Tut's Wah Wah Hut in Glasgow. McGee, due to a mix-up in set times, heard Oasis play just four songs and promptly offered them a deal. "in the audience that night was Alan McGee, the head of creation records. All it took though was those four songs. He offered them a deal with creation, an indie label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Indie Rock: Part 4

podcast.title: Sony Bankrolling (1993)
podcast.body: In 1993, Sony was reportedly "bankroll[ing] Creation" Records, and the label's executives wanted to observe Oasis perform before officially signing the band. This led to Oasis performing at a Sony convention that year. "Because I think at the time Sony were a bankroll in creation and I think they wanted to have a look at us."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: I Did Not Know That

podcast.title: Acquisition by Sony
podcast.body: Creation Records was acquired by Sony at the precise moment Oasis was signing its recording contract. While this provided Oasis with significant major label backing and promotional power from the outset, the band's initial discovery and support came from the independent spirit of Creation. "Sony compro clientes son recursos justo al tiempo en el que estaban firmando el contrato escoráfico de oasis."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: OASIS: Pilares del Brit Pop

podcast.title: Acquisition by Sony
podcast.body: To avoid complete collapse due to the financial strain imposed by "Loveless," Creation Records was acquired by Sony months after the album's release. This acquisition injected much-needed funds, allowing the label to continue investing in new, emerging bands. "Y toda esta audiencia valió la pena, pues depende de que me preguntes claro, para mí, y para todos los que amamos el disco, la respuesta es un rotundo sí."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: El disco imposible: La historia de Loveless y My Bloody Valentine

podcast.title: Acquisition by Sony and Discovery of Oasis
podcast.body: Creation Records was acquired by Sony in the early 1990s. Following this acquisition, Creation Records embarked on an intensive search for new stars and discovered Oasis in 1993, a band that at the time had no material released. Sony then placed a huge bet on Oasis's launch. "justo una de las grandes estrellas que descubriría Crisson Records justo cuando es comprada por Sony y eso asis. Tras la compra por Sony, Crisson empieza a una búsqueda o sesiva de nuevas estrellas, una de las que consigue eso asis que aún no había tenido ningún tipo de material, estamos hablando del 93 y Sony ha puesto muerte por el lanzamiento de base."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: El BRIT POP como negocio discográfico

podcast.title: Alan McGee's Direct Discovery and Signing
podcast.body: Alan McGee, the head of Creation Records, famously signed Oasis "more or less on the spot" after witnessing their impromptu performance at King Tuts Wawa Hut. His initial step to promote the band involved releasing a simple 12-inch single with a plain white label, which he "slipped it to a variety of people within the industry, hoping to drum up some hype," a strategy that successfully launched Oasis's career. "he was so impressed with the boys from Manchester, the Oasis boys, that he decided more or less on the spot to sign him up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 7

podcast.title: Bankrupted by My Bloody Valentine's Loveless
podcast.body: My Bloody Valentine's album "Loveless" took two years to produce and was so costly that it literally bankrupted Creation Records, despite becoming a seminal work that influenced countless bands. "My Bloody Valentine spent two years making an album called Lovelace, that literally bankrupted Creation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: British Independent (Indy) Label
podcast.body: Creation was identified as an example of a British independent label, part of the group referred to as "Indy" in the UK. These labels were characterized by their standalone nature, maintaining complete independence from major multinational record companies. "And this list included mute and factory and rough trade and creation and dozens more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Etymology: Part 1

podcast.title: Discovery of My Bloody Valentine
podcast.body: Creation Records was the independent label that originally discovered My Bloody Valentine, establishing a reputation for finding new talent. "Crisson Records era la discográfica que había finalmente descubierto a MyBlood y Valentin"

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: El BRIT POP como negocio discográfico

podcast.title: Discovery of Oasis
podcast.body: Creation Records, through its representative Alan McGee, allegedly discovered the band Oasis at King Tuts Wah Wah Hut in Glasgow, Scotland, on May 31, 1993. This discovery supposedly occurred after Oasis threatened the venue owner with arson if they were not permitted to play. "Oasis was discovered by Alan McGee of creation records after they allegedly threatened the owner with arson if he didn't let them play that night."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Listener Email

podcast.title: Discovery of The Jesus and Mary Chain
podcast.body: This label signed The Jesus and Mary Chain after their demo tape was brought to the attention of label head Alan McGee. Creation Records then released their surprise hit single "Upside Down" and their debut album *Psycho Candy*. "Their demo tape came to the attention of Alan McGee and an indelabel called Creation Records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Shoegaze

podcast.title: Financial Challenges and Sale
podcast.body: Creation Records experienced financial difficulties despite its successes. Notably, one of My Bloody Valentine's records was so expensive to produce that it "nearly bankrupted the label." Alan McGee eventually sold Creation Records to Sony. "Despite its successes, Creation did have its money issues like a lot of these other labels, especially after one of McGee's proudest signings, my bloody Valentine, turned in a record that was so expensive to make that it nearly bankrupted the label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 9

podcast.title: Financial Crisis Caused by "Loveless"
podcast.body: The exorbitant and protracted production of My Bloody Valentine's "Loveless" album brought Creation Records to the verge of bankruptcy. The album's estimated cost, over £150,000 according to Melody Maker, drained the label's funds, leading to a financial crisis that required drastic measures. "Lo que es cierto es que el disco llevó al borde de la quiebra Creation Records, y en eso, para no desaparecer, fueron comprados por Sony traslornos meses después."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: El disco imposible: La historia de Loveless y My Bloody Valentine

podcast.title: Founded by Alan McGee
podcast.body: Creation Records was a label founded by Alan McGee, who was notable for discovering Oasis. McGee later established a new label, Pop Tones, to which he signed The Hives. "Now, you might remember him as the founder of Creation Records and the guy who discovered a Vicious."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: Founded by Alan McGee
podcast.body: Creation Records was founded in 1983 by Scotsman Alan McGee, who was tired of the synth-based music prevalent at the time and desired to release material that resonated more with the raw promise of the Sex Pistols. "Another company who was right there was Creation, founded by Scotsman Alan McGee in 1983. He grown bored with the synth-based music of the time and decided to form a label that would release stuff that he liked, material that sounded more like the promise of the sex pistols."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Founding and Indie Niche
podcast.body: Creation Records was a "fascinating British indie label" founded by Alan McGee in 1983. It successfully carved out an important niche within the early 1980s indie movement, similar to labels like Mute, Rough Trade, Factory, and Two-Tone. "Another fascinating British indie label of the 80s was Creation. It was founded by a Scotsman named Alan McGee in 1983."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 9

podcast.title: Home of Influential Noisy Pop
podcast.body: Creation Records was a British label known for its "noisy pop bands" like My Bloody Valentine and Ride, which were significant influences on Sloan's album "Smeared." "all those sort of noisy pop bands that were on creation records and everything."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Independent Talent Discovery
podcast.body: Creation Records was an independent record label celebrated for its ability to discover and champion influential bands, notably My Bloody Valentine, and crucially, Oasis in 1993. It was Creation that initially believed in and invested in Oasis, long before any major label involvement. "A Oasis lo descubre clientes son recursos en 1993... era una discurafiga independiente."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: OASIS: Pilares del Brit Pop

podcast.title: Influential British Indie Label
podcast.body: Creation Records is cited as an influential British indie label, grouped with Factory Records and Sarah Records, for its instrumental role in shaping the identity of the British indie sound and style, especially in the context of the C86 movement. "Like factory records, creation, and a few others, Sarah Records helped bring an identity to the British indie sound and style, exemplified by the whole C86 movement."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Twee Pop: A History

podcast.title: Key Role in Indie Music and Artist Development
podcast.body: Creation Records played a crucial role in the independent music scene, launching the careers of influential bands such as Jesus and Mary Chain, Primal Scream, Ride, and Slowdive. By 1988, it was a recognized and respected label within the underground music community. "Juega una discográfica clave para entender las cenain di. Lanzando la carrera de bandas como Jesus and Mary Chain, Reimel Scream, Wright o Slowdive."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: El disco imposible: La historia de Loveless y My Bloody Valentine

podcast.title: Near Bankruptcy from Loveless
podcast.body: My Bloody Valentine's 1991 album *Loveless* was recorded over two years in 19 different studios, an exceptionally expensive undertaking that "nearly bankrupted their record label." This demonstrates the label's commitment to the band's ambitious artistic vision, despite the financial strain. "And it was so expensive that it nearly bankrupted their record label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Shoegaze

podcast.title: Oasis's Indie Label
podcast.body: Creation was the "small indie label" that Oasis impressed with their swagger, leading to their debut album recording. "After impressing the owner of a small indie label called Creation with their swagger, Oasis recorded a debut album that was at once new and familiar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

podcast.title: Oasis's Rise on a "Has-Been" Label
podcast.body: Creation, described as a "formerly has been" label, became the home of Oasis, who then grew into one of the biggest bands in the world during the Britpop era. This demonstrates the capacity of indie labels, even those with past struggles, to achieve global prominence, particularly within the UK music scene. "Meanwhile, Oasis became one of the biggest bands in the world while part of the roster of a formerly has been label called Creation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Definition (from the vault)

podcast.title: Post-Acquisition Success with Oasis
podcast.body: Following its acquisition by Sony, Creation Records received a financial injection that enabled it to continue backing new talent. This allowed them to sign the then-unknown Oasis, who subsequently spearheaded the Britpop movement. Oasis's second album, "(What's the Story) Morning Glory?", became the best-selling British album of the decade, marking a significant success for the label under Sony. "Sony les dio una injección de dinero para seguir apostando por mandas noveles. Ficharon a unos desconocidísimos o asis, quienes se convirtieron en los abandonados de este nuevo genero que iba a arrasar en los años 90. El Britpop, eso segundo álbum, Watch the Story, Modern Glory, se convirtió en el disco británico más vendido de la década."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: El disco imposible: La historia de Loveless y My Bloody Valentine

podcast.title: Prominent on C86 Cassette
podcast.body: Creation Records was one of the indie labels whose artists were featured on the influential C86 cassette, a compilation that reflected the state of new music in Britain in 1986. "They tapped labels like Creation and Rough Tray and a bunch of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Signing Ride
podcast.body: After Jim Reed of The Jesus and Mary Chain passed along Ride's demo tape to Alan McGee, the head of Creation Records, the label promptly signed the Oxford-based band. This move brought one of the era's significant shoegaze acts to the label. "He signed them right up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Shoegaze

podcast.title: Signing of Oasis
podcast.body: Creation Records, headed by Alan McGee, signed Oasis after McGee accidentally witnessed their four-song set at King Tut's Wawa Hut in Glasgow on May 31, 1993. "This was the night Alan McGee, the head of creation records, accidentally showed up early and inadvertently against his will, caught the Oasis set. But it was enough for him to sign the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In the Studio with Oasis

podcast.title: Subdirector's Nervous Breakdown During "Loveless" Production
podcast.body: During the chaotic and financially draining production of "Loveless," Dick Green, the subdirector of Creation Records, suffered a nervous breakdown so severe that his hair turned white overnight, illustrating the immense stress and despair within the label's offices. "Mientras tanto, las oficinas de Creation, De Crisidil, su subdirector, sufrió una crisis nerviosa, tan intensa que se le pone el pelo blanco de la noche a la mañana."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
